view.rationale: Management raised FY26 guidance and delivered several clear operational beats — stronger-than-expected backlog ($1.82B), revenue modestly above the implied bar, larger-than-forecast adj. EBITDA/margin expansion to mid-teens, strong FCF and rapid synergy capture — with no control-accounting caveats, making this a net positive for the stock.

Q2 missed revenue and fell short on the EBITDA floor (Adj. EBITDA $4.9M vs. the ~ $5.5M arithmetic minimum), and management cut FY EBITDA guidance materially — a clear negative; partially offset by a signed extension of the term loan and improved liquidity, which removes the largest tail risk.

Revenue modestly beat consensus and, critically, backlog rose a large 17.4% sequentially to $246.1M (with management saying ~80% will convert), while guidance was reaffirmed — a constructive combo that should drive a positive reaction despite a slight adj. EBITDA miss.

Net: largely a confirmation print with several previously-known positives (full enrollment, Novo supply deal, patent allowance) and a better-than-expected cash balance (~$23.9M) that reduces near-term dilution risk; offset by management reiterating that additional financing will likely be needed to reach the full readout, leaving upside limited but skewed positive.

Ferguson beat on revenue and EPS, printed stronger-than-expected margins, and raised FY guidance (narrowing the low end of the margin range), plus announced the accretive FloWorks deal — a combination likely to produce a strong positive reaction, though higher leverage and weaker H1 cash flow temper upside.

Management cut FY ARR and revenue guidance materially below prior guide/consensus and printed weaker-than-expected Q2 ARR and renewal rates (UEM/EDR pressure), offset only partially by cost cuts and stable adj. EBITDA — a clear growth disappointment that should drive a negative next-day reaction.

Big negative surprise: a sizable Q2 revenue shortfall plus a ~15% midpoint cut to FY26 revenue, a $26.9M goodwill impairment and a slip of cash-flow breakeven into 2027 (year-end cash now ~ $80M) drive a material downside; limited positives (lower-than-expected cash burn and a senior commercial hire/reorg) only partially offset the hit.

Revenue roughly inline with the analyst's base case but below consensus; management withdrew FY26 guidance and signaled material generic risk plus an immediate cash hit from a Hercules amendment and strategic-review process — a clear negative catalyst that was only partially anticipated.

Material cuts to FY27 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance (midpoint down ~3.5%) plus lower FCF and product/margin headwinds drive a negative reaction, partially offset by a much-stronger-than-expected South Africa ARR acceleration and an optimistic Q4 exit run-rate comment.

Slight revenue and EPS misses and a materially higher-than-expected SG&A (plateauing at ~$208M) are offset by strong Auvelity script growth/prescriber activation, first quantified ADA launch metrics, and a healthier-than-feared cash balance (~$320M); net effect = modestly negative near-term sentiment but not a rout.

The quarter largely matched the pre-announced P&L (revenue ~35M, EPS ~$0.04) and reiterates the raised FY revenue guide, but materially weaker-than-expected orders (28.9M) and a lower backlog ($45.4M) are the key negatives; stronger semi orders and a sizable cash build limit downside, yielding a mildly negative near-term reaction.

Revenue and royalties slightly beat the note while management materially raised FY26 revenue and operating-income targets (and reported margin expansion), plus a major NPU customer win — a clear positive vs the base case and should drive an above-average next-day return.

The financials were pre-filed and the call largely confirmed expected items (ETH holdings, buybacks, Galaxy fund, cash build) with no new mNAV-linked buyback policy or forward guidance; GAAP losses and impairments were already public and thus not market-moving. Absent a concrete capital-allocation commitment, the stock should see a muted reaction with ETH price action driving next-day moves.

Big upside on top-line: TONMYA drove a materially higher-than-expected Q2 ($11M of $13.5M total) with strong scripts and unusually high net revenue per script, plus refill strength. Offsetting but not negating the beat: management left runway only into early Q2'27 (dilution risk remains), so upside is meaningful but capped by near-term funding overhang.

The print beats on revenue, GMV, take rate (6.47%), adj. EBITDA ($7.9M and $27M TTM) and produced positive EPS — clearing the $25M run-rate and buyback signal — but gross margin contracted ~260bps (FFL startup costs) and management warned the Virginia-driven demand tailwind may not repeat, tempering forward visibility.

Q2 beat on revenue/Adj. EBITDA and materially raised FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance (to $410–420M / $85–95M) plus outsized WHS revenue and margins and a larger pipeline — outweighs a modest increase in capex guidance; this is a high-positive catalyst for the stock.

Q1 delivered a clear top- and bottom-line beat plus several structural positives (new U.S.–Jordan duty-free agreement, a $5M Urban Outfitters win, and a stronger order outlook from the largest customer). The near-term offset is management's Q2 margin guide cut to ~14–15% due to transport costs, which tempers but does not outweigh the substantial positive newsflow.

Big negative: management deconsolidated/transacted the transit & tolling businesses, producing a large continuing-ops revenue shortfall and a material FY revenue/EBITDA downgrade. Positives (strong sale multiple, proceeds earmarked for debt paydown, materially lower net leverage) blunt but do not offset the guidance cut and Q2 EBITDA miss, so expect a weak near-term market reaction.

Small revenue/EBITDA beat and definitive Idaho-Falls sale provide clarity and support the story, but commercial mix deterioration and limited deleveraging/retained-EBITDA from the sale blunt the upside; guidance was simply reaffirmed ex‑Idaho, so upside is modest and mostly priced in.

Fee-related earnings slightly exceeded the preview (FRE $50M, 45% margin), AUM and fee-paying AUM came in ahead of the base case (AUM $97B / fee-paying $78B), and the unexpected in-quarter close of the ~$1.2B credit secondaries fund plus a large SpaceX mark meaningfully uplifted unrealized carry — all of which should produce a modestly positive day despite total revenue and EPS lines not being explicitly disclosed.

Revenue comfortably beat the consensus/whisper and management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA (midpoint up ~7%), plus buyback acceleration and strong Q3 guide; offset slightly by a $2.5M revenue trim from phasing out a low-margin resale stream. Net = positive, guidance-driven outcome.

RadNet beat revenue and delivered record adj. EBITDA, raised imaging guidance and showed stronger-than-expected same-center volumes and DH ARR progress — all positive vs the preview. Much of the positive outcome was anticipated, so upside should be solid but not extreme; EPS was not reported in the facts, which tempers conviction.

Revenue and EPS beat consensus and OCF/H1 liquidity were materially better than feared, but management merely reiterated FY guidance (a raise was priced in) and raised FY capex meaningfully while EBITDA came in below the house estimate — net is a modestly negative reception.

Company maintained FY guidance and delivered some positives (45Z capture, D3 > assumed, FSS recovery), but revenue and GAAP EPS missed and adjusted EBITDA sat at the low end of the implied run-rate while liquidity fell—so the credibility question remains and the near-term reaction should be modestly negative.

Clear positive operational beat: same-store occupancy and RevPOR in-line-to-better, NOI margin slightly above the analyst base, Adj. EBITDA modestly ahead and normalized FFO positive; critically, the bridge was refinanced (material binary resolved) and management committed to issuing full-year normalized FFO guidance for 2027 — all supportive, though lack of quantified synergies limits upside.

Adjusted EBITDAX ($338M) landed in our base-case range (below the company’s $370–410M guide), so the price-driven shortfall was largely priced in; however, unexpected positives — a value-accretive pipeline acquisition, faster/greater-than-expected Berry synergies, drilling-efficiency driven capex reductions (fewer rigs) and debt refinancing savings — offset headline weakness. The lack of buybacks and no clear FY EBITDAX/FCF re‑rate keeps upside limited, producing a modestly positive near-term reaction.

Top-line and EBITDA came in below the preview's base case (and well below the stale $30M consensus) and management admitted traffic headwinds persist, a clear near-term negative; those hits are partially offset by a closed three-year debt extension (removes near-term refinancing risk) and a cash-funded, accretive AI acquisition/rebrand, leaving a modestly negative market reaction likely.

Revenue missed consensus materially (-8.2%), GAAP gross margin weakened though adjusted gross margin (~20.2%) was inline with expectations; guidance was reaffirmed and Centric was disclosed (helpful but not quantified), while cash use and higher net bank debt are negatives — overall a mildly negative surprise set.

Top-line and adj. EBITDA materially missed the preview (Q2 sales down ~10% vs an expected ~$134M and adj. EBITDA $6.6M vs ~$11–12M), cash fell to ~$44M and international weakened — all negative for the levered equity. Reaffirmed FY26 guidance and a long-term >$600M target limit downside, so reaction should be negative but not catastrophic.

Top-line and consumables/flow-cell metrics materially exceeded the pre-release yardstick and FY guidance low end was nudged higher, while margin expanded; balance-sheet/runway still short of fully resolving the going-concern risk, so the reaction should be meaningfully positive but not a full de-risk re-rate.

Top-line materially beat consensus driven by a much-larger-than-expected CMS ($30.5M) and a >$125M CMS run rate, with media margins widening to the mid-30s and adjusted EBITDA materially better than modeled. Offsetting caps on upside: cash fell meaningfully and there was no removal of the going-concern/liquidity overhang.

Modest revenue beat and an upward guide (midpoint above Street) plus a materially better-than-expected gross margin and pulled-forward delirium commercialization/NTAP momentum are the primary positives; offset by a wider GAAP loss, lower cash than modeled, and many elements (raise, NTAP) were already anticipated — net: modestly positive near-term reaction.

Large revenue beat (Attruby strength) + clear NDA/PDUFA dates, strong kidney-protection and RWE data, and a $1B preferred close that materially derisks financing — together should drive a meaningfully positive next-day reaction.

Revenue and EBITDA missed the preview, subscription metrics deteriorated more than expected, and management withdrew guidance while liquidity is tight (low cash, revolver drawn), leaving the financing/capital-structure story unresolved — a net negative for equity given the delisting/timewall risk. The only clear positive was confirmation of the $628.4M escrow redemption (in July), but it arrives post-quarter and doesn't immediately ease Q2 liquidity pressure.

Large revenue miss and a sharply wider net loss (driven by $12.3M warrant FV losses and slipped customer deployments) outweigh positives — stronger chipset shipments (>5,100), a $30.2M cash balance, secured wafer capacity and an expanded ATM. Net: modest-to-materially negative share reaction expected given the disparity between operating/recurring revenue weakness and liquidity relief.

Revenue missed materially (-5% vs $24.6M cons.) and management walked back Q4 breakeven to merely targeting positive FCF, while cash plunged to ~$5.3M — these guidance and liquidity hits dominate the tape. Cost cuts, a modest EPS beat and the LTV/CAC disclosure are helpful but insufficient to offset the revenue/guidance shock.

The print largely matched the preview: cash and burn were the key metrics and both came in at/above the high end of the modeled range ($47.1M cash, lower burn), with management saying no raise planned before pivotal data; clinical durability and powered pivotal metrics were reiterated — together this reduces near-term financing risk and should produce a modestly positive reaction.

Company reaffirmed the $800M EBITDA guide (inline with the pre-release) and delivered a slightly better-than-midpoint Q2 EBITDA and stronger Digital Audio / positive FCF, but Multiplatform revenue and EBITDA disappointed and the Q3 guide midpoint (~$200M) is well below the ~$230M the note said was needed to make the H2 bridge — net outcome is mildly negative-to-neutral.

Material revenue and pro‑forma system‑wide sales beat, plus a well‑above‑expected adj. EBITDA and adj. EPS outturn, signal a clear operational inflection; no new guidance was given so the market will focus on the strong print and margin leverage.

Revenue, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS materially beat the pre-release/consensus (EBITDA well above the back-solved ~$10.2M), and management closed liquidity gaps with an upsized credit facility and a definitive Sea Ray acquisition (accretive). These operational and financing positives were not fully priced in, so expect an above-median positive reaction, though guidance detail remains limited and governance/material-weakness issues persist.

Mixed print: revenue slightly missed but adjusted operating income and margins materially exceeded the implied consensus (AOI beat and 390bps y/y margin expansion), plus stronger cash flow and faster deleveraging; offset by SDC delivery/backlog deterioration and a small revenue beat/miss mix and no FY guidance until November.

Management materially raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA to $80–110M (midpoint $95M), well above the prior $20–60M framework, and reported better-than-expected medical cost trend and a small revenue beat; the raise (despite much of Q2 EBITDA being payer settlements) is the primary bullish driver, partially offset by tight liquidity (only $21M cash).

Revenue modestly beat consensus and, crucially, adjusted EBITDA margin and adjusted EPS materially exceeded the pre-print base case (management had signaled a sequential margin step-down). Strong OCF/FCF and association traction reinforce the beat; the remaining event risk centers on management’s specifics for use of the $109M proceeds in the Q&A.

Headline revenue missed consensus (~−5%) and management cut FY revenue guidance (~−9.5% midpoint); those negatives likely outweigh the upside of a positive adj. EBITDA print and a 470bp gross-margin expansion (helped by a $5.3M tariff refund), leaving a modestly negative next-day reaction driven by increased refinancing risk.

Revenue materially beat consensus and management raised FY revenue guidance while gross margin improved to roughly breakeven and cash burn meaningfully slowed — positives that outweigh the absence of an explicit Texas cash confirmation and the one‑time nature of large recoveries. Overall this is a net-positive print that should provoke an above‑median, potentially sizable rally, though some upside is already reflected in whispers.

The print delivered transformational commercial wins (191 MW 20‑yr AI lab lease + AMD = 241 MW / ~$520M avg annual revenue, Corsicana LOI) and materially stronger liquidity/financing, which should re-rate the equity despite a wider-than-expected GAAP loss and weaker mining unit economics; net effect should be strongly positive.

Revenue beat the $4.7–5.15M consensus and backlog printed much higher (~$42.5M vs. ~$16M), and management initiated FY26 revenue guidance that implies total revenue above street consensus — these are material positives; EPS is dominated by mark-to-market items and margins were not explicitly improved, so upside is driven by revenue/backlog/guidance rather than profitability.

Revenue came in below the company/consensus guide driven by a sharp PRS decline and customer-concentration issues, and management withdrew FY26 guidance; partially offset by a stronger-than-expected gross margin and international/Liquifix strength, so net reaction should be modestly negative.

A materially larger-than-expected revenue beat and a sharp raise to FY revenue guidance were offset by a gross-margin miss (below even the new guide) and a sequential backlog decline; next-day move will hinge on management's credibility on the H2 margin bridge and the explanation that BASX booking weakness is just timing/lumpiness.

Company beat revenue, EPS and ARR vs. the pre-release guide and materially raised FY operating income while showing a clean cash position to address the 2027 converts; partially offset by continued ARR decline (core D&R slowed to ~5%) and a lower Q3 ARR guide, so the net effect is a notably positive surprise but not unambiguously transformational.

Management materially reduced deal uncertainty by disclosing Insitu is >$200M revenue, profitable and FCF-positive, while Q2 revenue sharply beat and adj. EBITDA landed at the better end of guide; most deal news was already partly priced in, so expect a positive but not extreme reaction.

Adj. EBITDA materially beat the guide and per‑unit profitability hit a record while the company reaffirmed FY guidance (and gave a constructive Q3 guide), offsetting a slight revenue shortfall versus the practical consensus and a pronounced 600bp unit‑growth drag plus a CFO departure; net result is modestly positive but mixed, hence a positive but not extreme reaction.

Mixed print: revenue materially missed consensus (~-12%) and management trimmed its company guidance range versus its prior 550–600M (negative), but the new midpoint (550M) sits above street consensus, gross margin/adj. EBITDA beat/held at ~12% and backlog/bookings were stronger than fears; net is a modestly negative near-term reaction.

Slight Q2 revenue miss (-~7.7%) and rising op-ex are offset by a reaffirmed FY guide, meaningful new government awards and a preliminary ~$1B J‑LEO award, plus a $1.15B low-coupon convertible that boosts pro forma cash >$3.7B — liquidity and large contract news should produce a modestly positive near-term reaction despite the miss.

Mixed print: materially stronger AUM growth and +$700M net inflows (unexpectedly positive) were offset by a revenue shortfall vs. consensus, a $19M unrealized loss from the Asian fund unwind (impairing future incentive income), weaker-than-expected adj. EBITDA/margins, and no new information on the strategic review — so likely a slightly negative-to-flat market reaction.

Very large revenue beat driven by Base Electron coming in well ahead of schedule, a modest raise to FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance, materially stronger bookings/backlog and a clean cash/debt position with a $50M buyback — all positive; litigation/related-party overhang remains but the operational confirmation should drive a strong near-term reaction.

Net outcome is mildly positive: Watkins and Brasada monetizations + a large SpaceX mark materially improve liquidity/NAV and validate capital-return optionality, while BKFC performance and lower holding costs are upside. Offsets are a $45M restaurant impairment, no Q2 buybacks, and new sports investments that siphon proceeds, leaving the print mixed but overall somewhat favorable.
Operational beat on EBITDA/EPS and improving NDR were offset by a tightened, lower FY26 revenue guide — the guide cut outweighs the quarter’s positives, leaving a modestly negative reaction expected.

Adj. EBITDA materially exceeded the high end of guidance and management raised FY26 revenue/EBITDA/EPS, which together are the primary positives likely to drive a strong next-day reaction; offset by Military+ registrations printing only at the low end of the guided range and a Q3 timing/marketing shift that tempers the outlook for near-term demand.

Revenue and reported bitcoin holdings/net financial assets materially exceeded the preview model and Truth API traction is stronger than anticipated, which reduces immediate solvency fears; but GAAP loss and operating expenses came in far worse than modeled and the critical Nov‑30 convertible put remains unresolved, so the next‑day move should be modestly positive but not decisively bullish.

Q2 delivered a clean operating beat (net income and adj. EBITDA above the guide high end) and revenue was inside the company range, but the print was offset by a sizable negative FCF/inventory build, weakening subscriber trends (no clear stabilization), and conservative Q3 guidance (initiated) with margin pressure in nutrition — a mixed report that should produce a muted-to-slightly-negative reaction.

Top-line and ATS revenue/op-profit modestly beat the pre-release base, but management warned Q2 was exceptional and guided to a sequential decline while ATS opex jumped and Media swung to a loss — a mixed print that should temper upside and produce a slightly below-median reaction.

The print offered a modestly constructive update to the strategic-review process (management says it's in later stages) and strong subscription metrics (record 69% attach), plus retail expansion — positives not fully anticipated. However, management reiterated withdrawal of guidance and provided no cash, covenant, or margin detail, leaving the key solvency/liquidity catalysts unresolved, so upside is limited.

Big positive read-throughs on the CPG pivot (run-rate raised to $35–40M, distribution ~2,000 doors, June >$2M) plus a nonbinding LOI to monetize U.S. restaurants materially outweigh a small revenue miss vs. stale consensus and an EPS/debt drag; sequential margin improvement and guidance reaffirmation further support a positive reaction.

Net negative: the FDA process just received an Additional Information letter requiring an SIR alignment meeting (risks delaying the ~Aug 22 de novo path), revenue came in well below management's prior ~$250K guide, and H2 cash-burn guidance was raised to ~$8M/qtr — increasing near-term dilution risk; modest positives (narrowing adj. EBITDA, MolDX coverage expansion) do not offset these headlines.

Revenue essentially met the low-confidence pre-release bar and management quantified Monovate (payments) at $5M while legacy swap volume held better than feared; however large one-time integration/transaction costs and ongoing European card-issuance constraints limit near-term upside.

Material top-line and adj. EBITDA beats plus a raised FY revenue guide and strong subscriber adds materially exceed the pre-call bar; large short interest should amplify upside even as legal accruals, negative FCF and ‘structurally lower’ margin commentary cap the move.

Revenue met the company’s pre‑announced $18.5M floor (so not a beat vs the effective yardstick) and guidance was reiterated, but materially better gross margin (49%) and a record positive adj. EBITDA, plus sizeable treasury/cash and ongoing buybacks, are unexpected positives that should produce a modestly positive next‑day reaction despite the reverse‑split/liquidity overhang.

Kopin delivered in-line-to-modestly-better revenue but reported several upside operational datapoints — product revenue implied >$7M, product gross margin turned positive (14%) and management signaled H2/ FY guidance upside with sizeable YTD orders — driving a constructive read despite EPS benefiting from one-offs and a weaker unrestricted cash balance.

The quarter materially missed on profitability and cash (negative adj. EBITDA and a large OCF swing) versus the soft consensus, but the market-positive developments — a larger forward sales book (~$2.4B), landmark capacity deals, and a reduced Turtle Creek cost / financing plan that avoids equity — should cap downside, leaving a modestly negative next‑day reaction.

Q2 delivered a modest revenue beat and EBITDA beat, while the key contribution ex‑TAC line came in essentially inline with guidance/our preprint — and Q3 contrib ex‑TAC guidance matches the bar the note set. Strong direct‑access/CTV traction and early Outcomes/TVision evidence are positives, but revenue guidance midpoint is a touch below our revenue lift expectation; net effect should be a muted-to-modestly positive reaction.

Modest beat to the analyst's low-revenue/eps model and better-than-feared gross margin, but cash burn, collapsing YTD volumes and no reinstated FY26 guidance leave solvency/visibility concerns unresolved — a mixed print that is mostly priced in.

Company missed Q2 revenue meaningfully and cut FY revenue below the previously disclosed $1.35B low end, delayed India launch, and took large non‑cash write‑downs — all material negatives; modest Prism.io deployment/scan acceleration and slightly improved core gross margin were the few positives, leaving a strongly negative near‑term reaction likely.

Company cut FY26 guidance materially (EPS midpoint down ~21%), reported a revenue and EPS miss, originations fell and net charge-offs rose to ~52%; BNC regulatory progress and a $40M buyback offer limited offset. Overall a clearly negative print dominated by worsening credit and a guide cut.

Management reaffirmed the FY26 guide (the key governance/valuation hinge) and delivered strong cash flow and early synergy capture, offsetting expected margin compression from the KUBRA mix; a small EBITDA miss keeps the print from being unambiguously bullish. Overall the quarter largely confirms the board's thesis and should produce a modestly positive market reaction rather than a decisive re-rate.

Top-line and Adj. EBITDA materially beat the pre-release anchors, Honey Birdette comps/retail beat expectations, licensing ex-Byborg cleared the $5.9M threshold, and a sizable share repurchase plus clearer net-debt path reduce tail risk — all positives that were not fully anticipated.

Revenue beat the $75M guidance, GAAP gross margin surprised materially higher (39.3%), adjusted EBITDA and non‑GAAP EPS came in well above expectations, and Q2 revenue guide was raised — offset only by a lower Q2 adjusted‑EBITDA guide due to planned investment and large one‑time GAAP charges.

Results show a material revenue collapse and wider losses/EBITDA deterioration, offset partially by a strengthened cash position from a recent raise, regulatory approval (NFA), and progress toward commercial launch; absent disclosed commercial terms or user metrics, the print leans negative but not catastrophic.

Quarter came in essentially in line on revenue but with a sizable EPS/Adj. EBITDA beat and margin expansion; those positives are offset by a trimmed FY top-end and weaker airway/AffloVest trends plus prior-auth timing shifting Medicare orders into Q3. Net is a modestly positive-but-mixed reaction driven by guidance tone rather than the headline quarter.

Revenue printed roughly inline with the prior guide/consensus, but multiple positives — a 41.5% non‑GAAP gross margin beat, a Q3 revenue guide whose midpoint is above street, a larger backlog/capture rate, a big cash raise, and the Iridium acquisition — should drive a constructive next‑day move; offset by weaker Q3 margin guidance (below the 38% threshold the note flagged), a tariff‑refund‑aided Q2 margin (lower quality), and larger negative free cash flow.

Top-line was essentially in-line with company guidance (within $105–110M) and revenue/unit beat (positive), but adjusted EBITDA materially missed expectations and the large Hansen & Adkins deal (financed with convert and increasing leverage) plus second-half OR guidance near ~97% and delayed synergies make this a mixed but modestly negative read for near-term returns.

Revenue materially exceeded the pre-release yardstick and management delivered the promised first formal guide (Q3 midpoint ~$90M), while segment disclosure, high GPU utilization and a Together AI deal underscored commercial traction; GAAP loss widened meaningfully from acquisition/transaction costs, keeping some skepticism about accounting noise and funding for the capex roadmap.

Q2 results beat the quarter-level EBITDA/ margin expectations, but management cut FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance materially below pre-release midpoints and reported weakening active clients/GSV and slowing AI-related growth — the guide cut will dominate sentiment and likely drive a negative reaction.

Quarter came in essentially in-line with the company guide (Q2 rev $29.5M; adj. EBITDA within range) and FY guidance was reaffirmed, but management added a constructive Q3 guide, clearer near-term SurfOS revenue cadence from Wheels Up, faster broker onboarding (29→50) and an additional working-capital tranche — plus debt amortization relief — which together should produce a modestly positive market reaction.

Operational metrics (Q2 TTV of $169M and cash down to $50.7M) materially missed the constructive ramp the market needed; the huge EPS print was driven by a Transchem fair-value re-measurement that the preview flagged as the likely source of any positive EPS, so the headline beat is largely already anticipated and unlikely to offset the operational disappointment.

Revenue materially beat the guide/consensus and management raised FY revenue growth, driven by strong APAC/China and NPI mix gains; however a 100bp cut to FY gross-margin guidance and a weaker cash balance (H1 cash burn) cap upside, leaving a positive but muted market reaction.

Big upside on cash/net-debt reduction and an unexpected profitable quarter (and a raise to FY26 EBITDA guidance) — evidence of land monetization traction — should drive a materially positive, above-average reaction despite the name's history of muted EPS sensitivity.

Q2 was effectively inline on revenue but showed several upside beats (5.2% cc revenue, adj. EBITDA topping guidance, GM expansion, advertising/Korea strength and new IP initiatives). Offsetting this, Japan weakness and a Q3 cc guide that still falls short of the acceleration needed for a clean ‘double-digit exit’ keep upside capped, so the print should be modestly positive but not market-movingly so.

Orders/backlog and record Air & Liquid profitability were confirmed (backlog slightly above the note), but revenue, consolidated adj. EBITDA and EPS missed the pre-release model and the key FCEP EBITDA recovery target (≈$9M) fell short; slim liquidity adds downside risk, so the net reaction should be modestly negative.

Print largely matched the preview: cash ~$9.5M and R&D stepped up as expected (supporting trial restarts). Negative items — an EPS miss (wider loss) and management saying INVINCIBLE-3 needs ~$30M incremental with current cash insufficient — raise dilution risk, leaving the net read neutral-to-slightly negative absent partnering or new financing.

Mixed print: revenue slightly missed and FY26 revenue guidance was trimmed (the headline negative), but EBITDA and EPS materially beat with raised EPS/EBITDA guidance, faster-than-expected deleveraging, and concrete Savannah River / nuclear partnership detail. The trade-off between a guidance-driven revenue cut and stronger profitability and balance-sheet progress supports a modestly positive, but not exuberant, post-earnings reaction.

Revenue came in just below the company guidance floor ($70.7M vs $71M) — the single biggest headline negative — while management nonetheless reiterated FY revenue and EBITDA guidance. Offsetting positives (strong Vevye prescriptions/market share, record AIHESO units and a 71% gross margin) temper the reaction, but the guidance‑floor miss + the pre-call vacuum make a near‑term negative price reaction most likely.

A large $337M pretax CM charge (‑$1.99 EPS) and a materially lower reported FY EPS midpoint ($4.05) dominate the print and should drive a negative re-rate, despite stronger-than-expected backlog/book-to-burn, International revenue/margin recovery, and a raised adjusted-EBITDA margin target.

Revenue and EPS modestly beat consensus while management raised organic-revenue guidance to 9–10% and materially sized Nexus (scope +40% and multi-site value), improving the growth optionality and keeping FY EPS/AOI ranges intact — a clearly positive, but partly anticipated, print.

Big operational beat: revenue modestly above consensus and adjusted EBITDA materially ahead ( ~$5.8M vs ~3.7M expected) with ~520bp gross-margin expansion and a reaffirmed FY26 guide — all supportive. Offset by meaningful negatives: independent GAC conversion cost estimates of $40–60M, no GAC sales expected in 2027, and very low quarter-end unrestricted cash, which cap the upside and keep the story mixed.

Management reaffirmed “substantially enrolled by year-end 2026” and mid-2027 interim timing, initiated the alternate-dosing FLEX study, and reported cash slightly above the prior range; the only notable surprise was a planned CEO succession and CFO replacement, so the print is broadly as expected and modestly positive.

Revenue missed materially vs the $6.07M consensus and management pushed the bulk of contracted ARR conversion into 2027 (not the H2 ramp the market wanted), which is negative; offsets include stronger-than-expected gross margins and a healthy pro-forma cash balance, so expect a sizable but not catastrophic negative reaction.

Two clear narrative beats (a fifth Stage‑3 customer added ahead of the 'by end of Q3' guide and an existing material supply/licensing agreement in place with a second under negotiation) outweigh otherwise inline revenue/EPS, so expect a meaningfully positive, milestone-driven reaction.

Management beat EPS materially but ~ $0.31 of the beat was a one‑time IEEPA tariff refund; crucially they raised FY27 EPS guidance well above Street and enlarged the buyback program, which should drive a positive near‑term reaction despite the revenue miss and lower FY27 adjusted FCF guidance.

Small revenue beat and a raise to the low end of FY26 guidance (new midpoint modestly above street); material $6M APAC Protector order and better EBITDA flow-through bolster the beat, partially offset by a smaller-than-expected NearLab 2H contribution and continued exclusion of AVCAD from guidance.

Top-line and margin materially beat expectations (higher revenue, 51% gross margin) and Adj. EBITDA turned positive with cash up after an ATM — all supportive; offset by worse-than-expected treatment-session declines and a slight trim to the FY revenue range plus commentary of choppier H2, leaving the covenant/financing story still unresolved.

Guidance was raised to the mechanically-expected $103–108M (midpoint ~$105.5) so the headline guide was largely priced in; positives (record utilization, slightly stronger Flatrock stub revenue, better-than-expected pro forma leverage and a bump to 55k organic deployments) tilt the print mildly positive, offset by a GAAP EPS miss from ~$3.3M transaction costs.

Revenue and EPS beat consensus (Q2 upside was largely timing), but management reaffirmed FY guidance so H2 cliff and cash/dilution concerns remain; the material positive is a signed 30 MW AMD definitive agreement (15 MW by end-2027) which improves the 2027 optionality and tilts the reaction mildly positive.

Q2 revenue slightly missed consensus and cash fell, but management gave materially stronger Q3 combined-company revenue and adj. EBITDA guidance (midpoint ~8% above the prior $15M run-rate), which should drive a positive reaction despite near-term cash/cash-quality questions.
